scenario: 给 5 万员工做跨法务/工程/财务文档的知识助手(RAG)，答案准不准、引用对不对，主要在 LLM 生成前就已由检索决定。
scenario_en: A RAG knowledge assistant for 50,000 employees over legal/engineering/finance docs, where answer accuracy and citation quality are decided by retrieval before the LLM generates a token.
q: 为什么说「检索质量是答案准确率的最大杠杆」，数据侧要定哪几件事？
q_en: Why is retrieval quality the biggest lever on answer accuracy, and what must the data side decide?
why: 检索决定喂给 LLM 的是不是对的、够不够的证据，答案和引用在 LLM 吐第一个 token 前就已被检索定型。数据侧四个决策——分块、嵌入管线、混合检索、索引重建——直接决定检索质量。
why_en: Retrieval decides whether the evidence fed to the LLM is correct and sufficient, so the answer and citations are set before the first token, and four data-side decisions — chunking, embedding pipeline, hybrid retrieval, index rebuild — govern it.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  D["原始文档"] --> P["结构感知解析"] --> C["分块"] --> E["嵌入(带版本)"] --> I[("向量索引+BM25")]
  Q["用户问题"] --> H["混合检索"]
  I --> H --> R["重排"] --> L["LLM 生成"]
options: 检索无关紧要，只要 LLM 够强就能答对，重心该放在选更大的模型
检索质量只影响响应速度，不影响答案对错
检索决定喂给 LLM 的证据对不对/够不够，答案在生成前已定型；数据侧要定分块/嵌入/混合检索/索引重建
只要把所有文档一次性塞进超长上下文窗口，就根本不需要检索
options_en: Retrieval doesn't matter; a strong enough LLM answers correctly, so focus on a bigger model.
Retrieval quality only affects latency, not answer correctness.
Retrieval sets whether the LLM's evidence is correct/sufficient, fixing the answer before generation; the data side decides chunking/embedding/hybrid retrieval/index rebuild.
Just stuff all documents into a huge context window and you need no retrieval at all.
optionExplanations: 喂错证据再强的 LLM 也会答错或幻觉，检索是上游地基，不是靠加大模型能绕过的。
检索错的是内容不是速度：命中错块直接导致答非所问和错误引用。
对；生成前检索就定了证据集，四个数据决策决定这套证据的质量，是 RAG 的真正主战场。
5 万员工的全量语料远超任何上下文窗口，且塞满会触发 lost-in-the-middle，仍需检索先选证据。
optionExplanations_en: Feed wrong evidence and even a strong LLM answers wrong or hallucinates; retrieval is the upstream foundation, not something a bigger model bypasses.
Retrieval errors are about content not speed: hitting wrong chunks directly causes off-topic answers and wrong citations.
Correct — retrieval fixes the evidence set before generation, and the four data decisions govern its quality, the real battleground of RAG.
A 50k-employee corpus dwarfs any context window and stuffing triggers lost-in-the-middle, so retrieval must still select evidence first.

termDefinitions.meaning: 检索增强生成：先检索相关文档块，再让 LLM 基于这些块生成有依据的答案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) retrieves relevant document chunks first, then has the LLM generate a grounded answer from them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 经典的词法检索排名函数，按词频/逆文档频率给精确关键词匹配打分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BM25 (Okapi Best Matching 25) is a classic lexical ranking function scoring exact keyword matches by term and inverse-document frequency.

scenario: 团队复盘一个上线后频繁答非所问的 RAG，发现根因出在切分文档的方式。
scenario_en: A team debugs a RAG that keeps answering off-topic in prod and traces the root cause to how documents are split.
q: 为什么说分块(chunking)是最容易搞砸、后果最重的一步？
q_en: Why is chunking the easiest step to get wrong and the most consequential?
why: 分块决定检索的最小单位：切得太碎丢上下文、切在句中造成语义断裂、把表格切散成无意义片段，都会让检索命中错误或不完整的块，是生产 RAG 的头号失效点。所以分块策略要显式选、不能默认。
why_en: Chunking sets retrieval's atomic unit: too small loses context, mid-sentence cuts break meaning, and split tables become meaningless fragments, all making retrieval hit wrong or incomplete chunks — the top production failure — so choose the strategy explicitly.
options: 分块决定检索最小单位：切碎丢上下文、切在句中断语义、表格切散→检索到错块，是生产头号失效点
分块只是技术细节，切多大都不影响检索结果
分块只影响存储成本，与答案质量无关
分块由 LLM 在生成时自动完成，不用提前设计
options_en: Chunking sets the retrieval unit: too small loses context, mid-sentence cuts break meaning, split tables fragment → wrong chunks retrieved, the top production failure.
Chunking is a mere detail; any chunk size gives the same retrieval result.
Chunking only affects storage cost, unrelated to answer quality.
Chunking is done automatically by the LLM at generation time, needing no upfront design.
optionExplanations: 对；块是检索的原子单位，切法直接决定命中的块完不完整、对不对，错在这里下游全错。
块大小直接改变语义完整性和命中率，绝非无关紧要。
分块首先影响的是检索到的内容质量，存储成本是次要的。
分块是摄取期的数据管线设计，LLM 生成时只用已切好的块，不会自己切。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the chunk is retrieval's atomic unit, so how you split directly decides whether the hit chunk is complete and correct; errors here cascade.
Chunk size directly changes semantic completeness and hit rate, far from irrelevant.
Chunking primarily affects retrieved content quality; storage cost is secondary.
Chunking is ingestion-time pipeline design; the LLM uses pre-cut chunks and doesn't split at generation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把文档切成用于嵌入和检索的小片段，切法决定检索的最小单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Chunking splits documents into small pieces for embedding and retrieval; the method sets retrieval's atomic unit.

scenario: 语料是同质的运维日志和报表，格式统一、段落规整，你要选分块策略。
scenario_en: The corpus is homogeneous ops logs and reports with uniform format and regular paragraphs; pick a chunking strategy.
q: 这种同质规整文本该用哪种分块策略，为什么？
q_en: Which chunking strategy fits this homogeneous, regular text, and why?
why: 用固定大小分块(256-512 token、约 50 overlap)：同质文本没有复杂结构，固定切分实现简单、索引复杂度低，overlap 缓冲少量句中断裂。文本越规整，固定切分的主要风险(句中切断)越小。
why_en: Use fixed-size chunking (256-512 tokens, ~50 overlap): homogeneous text has no complex structure, so fixed splitting is simple with low index complexity, and overlap buffers occasional mid-sentence cuts, whose risk shrinks the more regular the text.
tradeoff: 固定大小(简单、索引轻但可能句中切断) vs 语义/分层(更贵但保结构)
whenOtherWins: 若语料是混合格式(合同+邮件+表格)，固定切分会把结构切碎，应改用语义或分层分块。
options: 分层分块，给每段配 parent/child
语义分块，按嵌入相似度找边界
每篇文档整体不切，直接当作一个块
固定大小分块(256-512 token、约 50 overlap)：同质文本结构简单，切分省事、索引轻
options_en: Hierarchical chunking with parent/child per section.
Semantic chunking, finding boundaries by embedding similarity.
Don't split at all; treat each document as one chunk.
Fixed-size chunking (256-512 tokens, ~50 overlap): homogeneous text is simple, so splitting is easy and the index is light.
optionExplanations: 分层的 parent/child 是给超长结构化文档保上下文用的，同质日志上是过度设计。
语义分块要额外 NLP、块大小可变，同质规整文本用不上这份复杂度。
整篇不切会让块过大、稀释检索信号又挤占 LLM 上下文预算。
对；同质文本主要风险(句中切断)本来就小，固定切分最省事、索引最轻，是恰当选择。
optionExplanations_en: Hierarchical parent/child preserves context for long structured docs; on homogeneous logs it's over-engineering.
Semantic chunking needs extra NLP and variable sizes, complexity unused on homogeneous regular text.
Not splitting makes chunks too big, diluting the retrieval signal and eating the LLM's context budget.
Correct — mid-sentence risk is already small on homogeneous text, so fixed splitting is simplest with the lightest index.

termDefinitions.term: fixed-size chunking / 固定大小分块
termDefinitions.meaning: 按固定 token 数切块并留少量重叠，简单但可能在句中切断。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fixed-size chunking splits by a fixed token count with small overlap — simple but may cut mid-sentence.

termDefinitions.meaning: 相邻块共享的一小段文本，用来缓冲被切断的句子。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Overlap is a shared span between adjacent chunks that buffers sentences cut at the boundary.

scenario: 知识库是混合格式(产品手册+FAQ+邮件)，同一库里文档长短和结构差异很大。
scenario_en: The KB is mixed-format (product manuals + FAQs + emails) with widely varying document lengths and structures.
q: 混合格式知识库该用哪种分块策略？
q_en: Which chunking strategy fits a mixed-format knowledge base?
why: 用语义分块：按句子/段落/嵌入相似度找自然边界，让每块语义完整，适配长短不一的混合格式。代价是块大小可变、要额外 NLP 预处理。
why_en: Use semantic chunking: find natural boundaries by sentence/paragraph/embedding similarity so each chunk is semantically complete, fitting the varied mixed formats, at the cost of variable chunk sizes and extra NLP preprocessing.
tradeoff: 语义分块(块语义完整但大小可变、需 NLP) vs 固定大小(简单但易切断)
whenOtherWins: 若文档是同质规整文本，固定大小更省事；若是超长结构化合同，分层分块的 parent/child 更合适。
options: 固定大小分块，一刀切 512 token
语义分块：按句/段/嵌入相似度找自然边界，每块语义完整，适配混合格式
完全不分块，整库当一个向量
随机切分，反正检索会兜底
options_en: Fixed-size chunking, a flat 512-token cut.
Semantic chunking: find natural boundaries by sentence/paragraph/embedding similarity so each chunk is complete, fitting mixed formats.
Don't chunk at all; make the whole KB one vector.
Split randomly; retrieval will compensate.
optionExplanations: 一刀切 512 会在混合格式里频繁切断结构，短文档被硬拆、长文档丢边界。
对；按语义边界切让每块自洽，正好吸收混合格式里长短结构的差异，检索命中更完整。
整库一个向量无法定位到具体证据，检索退化为无。
随机切分制造大量语义断裂块，检索只会更差，没有兜底一说。
optionExplanations_en: A flat 512 cut repeatedly breaks structure across mixed formats, hard-splitting short docs and losing boundaries in long ones.
Correct — cutting at semantic boundaries makes each chunk self-contained, absorbing the varied lengths and structures for more complete hits.
One vector for the whole KB can't localize evidence, degrading retrieval to nothing.
Random splitting creates many broken chunks and only worsens retrieval; there is no fallback.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按句子/段落/嵌入相似度的自然语义边界切块，块大小可变。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Semantic chunking splits at natural semantic boundaries (sentence/paragraph/embedding similarity), giving variable chunk sizes.

scenario: 文档是超长结构化的合同和手册，既要检索命中精确到段落，又要给 LLM 足够上下文。
scenario_en: Documents are long, structured contracts and manuals; hits must be precise at the paragraph level while giving the LLM enough context.
q: 这类超长结构化文档该用哪种分块策略？
q_en: Which chunking strategy fits long, structured documents?
why: 用分层分块：parent=章节/页、child=段落；用 child 做检索匹配保证精度，命中后返回 parent 给 LLM 补足上下文。既精确又不丢背景，代价是索引更大、要遍历父子关系。
why_en: Use hierarchical chunking: parent = section/page, child = paragraph; match on children for precision, then return the parent for LLM context — precise without losing background — at the cost of a larger index and parent-child traversal logic.
tradeoff: 分层(精度+上下文兼得但索引大、逻辑复杂) vs 单层(简单但精度与上下文二选一)
whenOtherWins: 若文档短小或同质，分层的父子结构是过度设计，固定或语义分块就够。
options: 固定大小分块，一刀 512
语义分块，按相似度切
分层分块：parent=章节/页、child=段落；child 匹配保精度，返回 parent 补上下文
每页当一块，不分父子
options_en: Fixed-size chunking, a flat 512.
Semantic chunking by similarity.
Hierarchical chunking: parent = section/page, child = paragraph; match children for precision, return parent for context.
One chunk per page, no parent/child.
optionExplanations: 一刀 512 在长合同里既可能切断条款，又无法在命中后带回整节上下文。
语义分块保完整但仍是单层，命中一块难同时给出所在章节的完整背景。
对；child 精确匹配 + 返回 parent 补背景，正好同时满足「命中要准」和「上下文要全」。
每页一块太粗，段落级的精确命中和引用都做不到。
optionExplanations_en: A flat 512 may cut clauses in long contracts and can't bring back the whole section's context on a hit.
Semantic chunking is complete but still single-level, so one hit can't also supply the full surrounding section.
Correct — precise child match plus returning the parent satisfies both 'precise hit' and 'full context' at once.
One chunk per page is too coarse for paragraph-level precise hits and citations.

termDefinitions.meaning: 父块=章节/页、子块=段落；用子块匹配保精度、返回父块补上下文。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hierarchical chunking uses parent = section/page and child = paragraph, matching on children for precision and returning parents for context.

scenario: 面试官要你比较三种分块策略，想看你能否按语料类型选。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks you to compare the three chunking strategies, checking whether you can pick by corpus type.
q: 固定/语义/分层三种分块在语义完整性、索引复杂度、适用语料上如何对比？
q_en: How do fixed/semantic/hierarchical chunking compare on completeness, index complexity, and corpus fit?
why: 固定简单但语义完整性低；语义保完整但要 NLP、块大小可变；分层最保上下文但索引最重。启发式：同质用固定、混合用语义、超长结构化用分层，面试要显式说出这条映射。
why_en: Fixed is simple but low-completeness; semantic preserves completeness but needs NLP with variable sizes; hierarchical best preserves context but has the heaviest index — heuristic: homogeneous → fixed, mixed → semantic, long structured → hierarchical, stated explicitly.
tradeoff: 语义完整性 vs 索引复杂度：固定轻但碎、分层全但重

rows: 超长结构化文档(合同/手册)

options: 三种没区别，随便选一种就行
分层最简单、固定最复杂，与语料类型无关
固定语义完整性最高，分层最低
固定简单低完整性适合同质；语义高完整性适合混合；分层最高完整性但索引重，适合超长结构化
options_en: The three are the same; pick any.
Hierarchical is simplest and fixed most complex, unrelated to corpus.
Fixed has the highest completeness and hierarchical the lowest.
Fixed is simple, low-completeness for homogeneous; semantic is high-completeness for mixed; hierarchical is highest-completeness but index-heavy for long structured docs.
optionExplanations: 三者在完整性、索引成本、适用语料上都不同，选错会直接拉低检索质量。
说反了：固定最简单、分层最复杂，且策略要按语料类型选。
颠倒了：固定完整性最低、分层最高。
对；这条「同质固定/混合语义/长结构分层」的映射正是面试要显式说出的启发式。
optionExplanations_en: The three differ on completeness, index cost, and corpus fit; choosing wrong directly lowers retrieval quality.
Backwards: fixed is simplest and hierarchical most complex, and the strategy tracks corpus type.
Reversed: fixed has the lowest completeness and hierarchical the highest.
Correct — this 'homogeneous→fixed, mixed→semantic, long-structured→hierarchical' mapping is the heuristic to state explicitly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分块方案给索引带来的大小与检索逻辑负担，分层最重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Index complexity is the size and retrieval-logic burden a chunking scheme adds to the index; hierarchical is heaviest.

scenario: 不管选哪种分块策略，都要先做一步文档解析。
scenario_en: Whatever chunking strategy you pick, a parsing step must come first.
q: 为什么「结构感知解析」是所有分块策略的前置必做项？
q_en: Why is structure-aware parsing a non-negotiable prerequisite for every chunking strategy?
why: 结构感知解析先识别表格、嵌套标题、列表等文档结构；不做它就直接按字符切，表格会被切成无意义碎片、嵌套标题错位，后续再好的分块也救不回。它是分块前不可跳过的地基。
why_en: Structure-aware parsing first recognizes tables, nested headers, and lists; without it, character-level splitting fragments tables into meaningless pieces and misplaces headers, which no downstream chunking can recover — the non-skippable foundation before chunking.
options: 结构感知解析只是可选优化，跳过也不影响检索
先识别表格/嵌套标题/列表等结构，否则会被切成无意义碎片，是分块前不可跳过的地基
它只对固定大小分块有用，语义和分层不需要
它由 LLM 在生成时完成，不属于数据管线
options_en: Structure-aware parsing is optional; skipping it doesn't affect retrieval.
Recognize tables/nested headers/lists first, else they fragment into meaningless pieces — the non-skippable foundation before chunking.
It only helps fixed-size chunking; semantic and hierarchical don't need it.
It's done by the LLM at generation time, not part of the data pipeline.
optionExplanations: 跳过它，表格和嵌套标题就被切成碎片，检索命中的块本身就是坏的，影响很大。
对；先保住结构再切，才不会让表格/标题在源头就变成无意义片段，任何策略都依赖它。
三种策略都建立在解析出的结构之上，语义和分层反而更依赖正确的结构边界。
解析是摄取期数据处理，早于嵌入和索引，跟 LLM 生成无关。
optionExplanations_en: Skip it and tables and nested headers fragment, so the retrieved chunk is already broken — a big impact.
Correct — preserving structure before splitting keeps tables/headers from becoming meaningless fragments at the source; every strategy depends on it.
All three build on parsed structure, and semantic/hierarchical rely even more on correct structural boundaries.
Parsing is ingestion-time processing before embedding and indexing, unrelated to LLM generation.

termDefinitions.term: structure-aware parsing / 结构感知解析
termDefinitions.meaning: 分块前识别文档的表格、标题、列表等结构，避免它们被切成碎片。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Structure-aware parsing recognizes a document's tables, headers, and lists before chunking so they aren't fragmented.

scenario: 固定大小分块常取 256-512 token、约 50 token 的重叠。
scenario_en: Fixed-size chunking commonly uses 256-512 tokens with about 50 tokens of overlap.
q: 「256-512 token、~50 overlap」这些数字在设计里怎么用？
q_en: How are the '256-512 tokens, ~50 overlap' numbers used in design?
why: 这是经验区间不是公式：块太小丢上下文、太大稀释检索信号并挤占 LLM 上下文预算，256-512 是二者的折中；~50 overlap 让相邻块共享边界句，缓冲句中切断导致的语义丢失。
why_en: These are empirical ranges, not formulas: too small loses context, too large dilutes the retrieval signal and eats the LLM's context budget, so 256-512 is the compromise, and ~50 overlap shares boundary sentences to buffer mid-sentence cuts.
options: 是经验折中区间：太小丢上下文、太大稀释信号又挤占上下文预算；~50 overlap 缓冲句中切断
是放之四海皆准的硬性标准，所有语料都必须严格用 512、overlap 必须恰好等于 50
数字越大越好，应该尽量往 4096 调
只是要背的数字，没有任何设计含义
options_en: An empirical compromise: too small loses context, too large dilutes the signal and eats the context budget; ~50 overlap buffers mid-sentence cuts.
A universal hard standard: every corpus, regardless of domain, must use exactly 512 with overlap exactly 50.
Bigger is always better; push toward 4096.
Just numbers to memorize with no design meaning.
optionExplanations: 对，这组数字是拿实测调出来的平衡点：切得太碎信息不全，切得太宽又会把无关内容一起喂给模型、占掉生成配额，重叠留一截边界防止句子被拦腰砍断。
把这两个数字当成放之四海皆准的铁律是误解，运维日志和法务合同该用的块大小不一样，要按语料调，不是死守 512/50。
并非越大越好，块一旦膨胀到几千 token，检索命中的相关片段被无关内容稀释，还会挤占模型能看到的其它证据配额。
把这两个数字当成不用理会的背诵项是低估：块大小和重叠直接决定检索能不能命中完整语义，是需要按语料校准的设计参数。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — a tuned trade-off: too thin loses evidence, too wide buries the model in noise; overlap keeps sentences from splitting.
Treating 512/50 as universal misreads it — logs and contracts need different sizes, tuned per corpus, not fixed numbers.
Bigger isn't better: a chunk ballooned to thousands of tokens buries the relevant part and crowds out other evidence.
Calling these numbers arbitrary undersells them — size and overlap decide retrieval completeness, tuned per corpus.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型处理文本的最小单位，块大小和上下文预算都以 token 计。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A token is the model's smallest text unit; chunk size and context budget are both measured in tokens.

scenario: 嵌入管线把每个块过嵌入模型，得到一个稠密向量。
scenario_en: The embedding pipeline runs each chunk through an embedding model to get a dense vector.
q: 关于「每个块的嵌入向量」，有个必须从第一天就记住的性质是什么？
q_en: What property of each chunk's embedding must you remember from day one?
why: 每个向量都绑定产生它的嵌入模型——向量空间由模型定义，不同模型产生的向量不可比。所以要从第一天就把嵌入模型版本写进每个块的元数据，否则日后升级模型时无从区分、迁移极痛。
why_en: Every vector is tied to the model that produced it — the vector space is defined by the model, so vectors from different models aren't comparable — hence tag each chunk's metadata with the model version from day one, or a later upgrade becomes a painful migration.
options: 向量和模型无关，任何模型的向量都能混在一个索引里比相似度
向量只跟文本有关，换模型不影响
每个向量绑定产生它的模型，向量空间由模型定义，必须从第一天给每块打上模型版本标签
向量维度可以随时改，不用记模型
options_en: Vectors are model-independent; any model's vectors can share one index and be compared.
Vectors depend only on the text; swapping models doesn't matter.
Each vector is tied to its model, the space is model-defined, so tag every chunk with the model version from day one.
Dimensionality can change anytime; no need to record the model.
optionExplanations: 跨模型的向量空间不同，混在一起比相似度是无意义的，正是要避免的错误。
同一文本换模型会得到完全不同的向量，模型是决定向量的关键变量。
对；从第一天打版本标签，日后升级才能区分新旧向量、走平行索引迁移，省下痛苦。
维度由模型决定，随意改维度等于换了向量空间，必须记录模型。
optionExplanations_en: Cross-model spaces differ, so comparing mixed vectors is meaningless — exactly the mistake to avoid.
The same text yields totally different vectors under a different model; the model is the decisive variable.
Correct — tagging versions from day one lets a later upgrade distinguish old/new vectors and migrate via a parallel index, avoiding pain.
Dimensionality is model-defined; changing it arbitrarily changes the space, so the model must be recorded.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一段文本映射成的稠密向量，用向量距离衡量语义相似度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding is a dense vector a text maps to, with vector distance measuring semantic similarity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 由某个嵌入模型定义的坐标系；不同模型的空间不可直接比较。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A vector space is the coordinate system a given embedding model defines; spaces from different models aren't directly comparable.

scenario: 选嵌入维度：是 384 还是 1024，语料规模很大、检索延迟和存储都要算账。
scenario_en: Choose embedding dimensionality — 384 or 1024 — for a large corpus where retrieval latency and storage both matter.
q: 嵌入维度(384-1024)怎么权衡，更高维意味着什么？
q_en: How to weigh embedding dimensionality (384-1024), and what does higher mean?
why: 维度越高能编码越细的语义差别，但索引更大、存储和检索更贵；维度越低更省但表达力弱。按语料语义复杂度和索引成本预算折中，不是越高越好。
why_en: Higher dimensionality encodes finer semantic distinctions but makes the index larger and storage/retrieval costlier, while lower is cheaper but less expressive, so compromise by semantic complexity and index budget rather than maxing it out.
tradeoff: 高维(语义更细但索引大、更贵) vs 低维(更省但表达力弱)
whenOtherWins: 若语料语义简单、规模巨大且预算紧，低维(384)更划算；语义细腻、规模可控时才上高维(1024)。
options: 维度越高一定越好，直接选最高的
高维编码更细语义但索引更大更贵，低维更省但表达弱，按语义复杂度+成本折中
维度和成本无关，随便选一个
维度必须等于块的 token 数
options_en: Higher is always better; just pick the max.
Higher encodes finer semantics but a larger, costlier index; lower is cheaper but weaker — compromise by semantic complexity and cost.
Dimensionality is unrelated to cost; pick any.
Dimensionality must equal the chunk's token count.
optionExplanations: 高维在大规模语料上会显著抬高存储和检索成本，未必换来相称的检索收益。
对；维度是语义分辨率和成本的取舍轴，按语料复杂度和预算选，而非无脑取最高。
维度直接决定索引大小和检索开销，和成本强相关。
维度是模型输出属性，和块的 token 数没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: High dimensionality sharply raises storage and retrieval cost on a large corpus without necessarily matching retrieval gains.
Correct — dimensionality trades semantic resolution against cost, chosen by corpus complexity and budget, not blindly maxed.
Dimensionality directly sets index size and retrieval overhead, strongly tied to cost.
Dimensionality is a model output property, unrelated to a chunk's token count.

termDefinitions.meaning: 嵌入向量的长度；越高语义分辨率越细，索引也越大越贵。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dimensionality is the embedding vector's length; higher gives finer semantic resolution but a larger, costlier index.

scenario: 语料是法务/财务专业文档，通用嵌入模型(如 e5-large)在专业术语和条款语义上表现平平。
scenario_en: The corpus is legal/finance domain docs, and a general embedding model (e.g. e5-large) underperforms on specialized terms and clause semantics.
q: 通用嵌入模型在这种专业语料上不够好，该怎么办？
q_en: What do you do when a general embedding model underperforms on this domain corpus?
why: 用领域微调的嵌入模型：通用模型没见够法务/财务术语，语义相近的条款可能被嵌得很远；在领域语料上微调让专业术语的向量更贴合，显著提升检索相关性。代价是要有领域数据和微调成本。
why_en: Use a domain-fine-tuned embedding model: a general model hasn't seen enough legal/finance terms and may embed semantically close clauses far apart, whereas fine-tuning on domain data aligns specialized-term vectors and sharply improves retrieval relevance, at the cost of domain data and training.
tradeoff: 领域微调(专业检索更准但要数据+训练) vs 通用现成(零成本但专业术语弱)
whenOtherWins: 若语料就是通用日常文本、没有专业术语壁垒，现成通用模型(e5-large)够用，微调是多余成本。
options: 换个更大的通用模型就行，不用管领域
放弃嵌入，改用纯 BM25 词法检索
忽略这个问题，反正 reranker 会兜底补回来
用领域微调的嵌入模型：通用模型没见够专业术语，微调让术语向量更贴合，检索更准
options_en: Just switch to a bigger general model, ignore the domain.
Drop embeddings and use pure BM25 lexical retrieval.
Ignore it; the reranker will compensate.
Use a domain-fine-tuned embedding model: the general one hasn't seen enough specialized terms, and fine-tuning aligns their vectors for better retrieval.
optionExplanations: 更大的通用模型仍缺领域术语暴露，专业条款的语义关系照样对不齐。
纯 BM25 丢掉语义匹配，改述和近义查询会大量漏召回，不是对症的修法。
reranker 只能在检索召回的候选里排序，检索本身漏了就补不回来。
对；领域微调把专业术语的向量拉到正确的相对位置，是提升领域检索相关性的正解。
optionExplanations_en: A bigger general model still lacks domain-term exposure, so clause semantics stay misaligned.
Pure BM25 drops semantic matching and misses paraphrase/synonym queries — not the right fix.
A reranker only reorders retrieved candidates; if retrieval already missed it, it can't be recovered.
Correct — domain fine-tuning pulls specialized-term vectors to correct relative positions, the right fix for domain relevance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在领域数据上继续训练模型，让它更贴合本领域的术语和语义。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fine-tuning continues training a model on domain data so it better fits the domain's terms and semantics.

scenario: 你要在候选嵌入模型间做初筛，想有个公开可比的性能参照。
scenario_en: You want a public, comparable performance reference to shortlist candidate embedding models.
q: 选嵌入模型时，常用哪个公开基准作参照？
q_en: Which public benchmark is commonly used to reference embedding-model selection?
why: 用 MTEB 排行榜：它在检索、聚类、分类等多类任务上横向评嵌入模型，给一个可比的起点。但它是通用基准，最终还要在自己领域的 held-out 查询集上验证，不能只看榜。
why_en: Use the MTEB leaderboard: it benchmarks embedding models across retrieval, clustering, classification, and more, giving a comparable starting point, but it's general so you still validate on your own domain's held-out query set.
options: 用 MTEB 排行榜：多任务横向评嵌入模型，给可比起点，但最终要在自己领域验证
用 HumanEval，它是代码生成基准
直接看模型参数量，越大越好
没有公开基准可参考，只能靠猜
options_en: The MTEB leaderboard: benchmarks embedding models across tasks for a comparable start, but validate on your own domain finally.
HumanEval, a code-generation benchmark.
Just look at parameter count; bigger is better.
There's no public benchmark; you can only guess.
optionExplanations: 对；MTEB 给横向可比的起点，但它是通用榜，领域场景仍要用自己的查询集复核。
HumanEval 评的是代码功能正确性，跟嵌入检索质量无关。
参数量大不等于检索强，嵌入质量要看基准和领域表现，不是看规模。
MTEB 正是这个公开基准，说没有是错的。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — MTEB gives a comparable starting point, but it's a general leaderboard, so domain use still needs your own query set.
HumanEval measures code functional correctness, unrelated to embedding retrieval quality.
More parameters don't mean better retrieval; embedding quality is judged by benchmarks and domain performance, not size.
MTEB is exactly that public benchmark, so 'none' is wrong.

termDefinitions.meaning: 横向评估嵌入模型在检索/聚类/分类等多任务表现的公开排行榜。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MTEB (Massive Text Embedding Benchmark) is a public leaderboard ranking embedding models across retrieval, clustering, classification, and more.

termDefinitions.term: held-out query set / 留出查询集
termDefinitions.meaning: 一组不参与训练、用来验证检索质量的代表性查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A held-out query set is a set of representative queries kept out of training, used to validate retrieval quality.

scenario: 团队把嵌入模型从 v1 升到 v2，图省事把 v2 的新向量直接加进 v1 的旧索引里一起检索。
scenario_en: A team upgrades the embedding model v1→v2 and, to save effort, adds v2 vectors straight into the v1 index for joint retrieval.
q: 把 v1 和 v2 的向量混在同一个索引里会怎样？
q_en: What happens if you mix v1 and v2 vectors in one index?
why: 不同模型的向量空间不同→跨模型算余弦相似度没有意义→检索排序变成噪声，新旧向量的「距离」不可比，答案质量悄悄崩坏且难排查。正解是不混：建平行索引、整体切换。
why_en: Different models have different vector spaces → cross-model cosine similarity is meaningless → retrieval ranking becomes noise, since old/new distances aren't comparable, silently wrecking answers and hard to diagnose — the fix is not to mix, but build a parallel index and swap wholesale.
options: 没问题，向量就是向量，混着用还能省一次重建
向量空间不同→跨模型余弦相似度无意义→检索排序变噪声、质量悄悄崩；正解是建平行索引整体切换
只会让索引变大一点，相似度照常准确
v2 会自动把 v1 向量转换过来对齐，无需处理
options_en: No problem; a vector is a vector, and mixing even saves a rebuild.
Different spaces → cross-model cosine is meaningless → ranking becomes noise, quality silently breaks; fix is a parallel index swapped wholesale.
It just enlarges the index a bit; similarity stays accurate.
v2 auto-converts and aligns the v1 vectors, so nothing to do.
optionExplanations: 混用省的是一次重建，赔的是整套检索排序失真，得不偿失。
对；跨模型距离不可比会让排序变噪声，且退化隐蔽难查，必须平行索引整体切。
问题不在大小而在相似度失去意义，检索会实质变差。
没有自动对齐这回事，不同模型的向量空间无法互转。
optionExplanations_en: Mixing saves one rebuild but corrupts the whole ranking — a bad trade.
Correct — cross-model distances aren't comparable, turning ranking into noise, and the degradation is subtle and hard to trace, so swap a parallel index wholesale.
The issue isn't size but that similarity loses meaning, so retrieval materially worsens.
There's no auto-alignment; vector spaces from different models can't be interconverted.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用向量夹角衡量语义相近程度，仅在同一向量空间内有意义。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cosine similarity measures semantic closeness by vector angle, meaningful only within one vector space.

termDefinitions.meaning: 索引里向量因模型不一致而逐渐偏离，导致检索质量悄悄退化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Drift is the gradual divergence of index vectors from model inconsistency, silently degrading retrieval quality.

scenario: 要把生产 RAG 的嵌入模型从 v1 升级到 v2，不能让线上检索质量出问题。
scenario_en: You must upgrade a production RAG's embedding model v1→v2 without breaking live retrieval quality.
q: 嵌入模型升级该怎么安全落地？
q_en: How do you safely roll out an embedding-model upgrade?
why: 每块元数据打上模型版本→用 v2 重嵌整个语料建一个平行索引→在 held-out 查询集上验证召回/相关性达标→原子切换(蓝绿)，旧索引留作回滚。绝不在同一索引里混 v1/v2。
why_en: Tag each chunk's version → re-embed the whole corpus with v2 into a parallel index → validate recall/relevance on a held-out query set → swap atomically (blue-green), keeping the old index for rollback, and never mix v1/v2 in one index.
tradeoff: 平行索引+蓝绿切换(安全可回滚但要重嵌整库) vs 原地混用(省事但向量空间不一致、质量崩)
whenOtherWins: 若只是往同版本模型的索引里加新文档(模型没变)，用增量更新即可，不必整体重建。
options: 每块打版本标签→v2 重嵌建平行索引→held-out 查询集验证→原子蓝绿切换，旧索引留回滚
直接把 v2 向量加进旧索引，边跑边替换
停机几小时，清空重建，期间服务不可用
让 v1 和 v2 各占一半索引，查询时随机选一个
options_en: Tag each chunk's version → re-embed with v2 into a parallel index → validate on a held-out set → atomic blue-green swap, keep old for rollback.
Add v2 vectors into the old index and replace on the fly.
Take hours of downtime, wipe and rebuild, unavailable meanwhile.
Let v1 and v2 each hold half the index, picking one at random per query.
optionExplanations: 对；平行索引 + held-out 验证 + 原子切换 + 保留旧索引回滚，是零风险升级的标准四步。
边跑边替换就变成 v1/v2 混用，向量空间不一致，检索排序会失真。
停机违背零停机要求，5 万员工随时在用，不可接受。
随机选半个索引让结果不可复现、质量抖动，是更糟的做法。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — parallel index + held-out validation + atomic swap + keeping the old for rollback is the standard zero-risk upgrade.
Replacing on the fly mixes v1/v2 with inconsistent spaces, distorting ranking.
Downtime violates the zero-downtime need with 50k employees always using it — unacceptable.
Randomly choosing half an index makes results irreproducible and quality jittery — worse.

termDefinitions.meaning: 备好两套环境，线上服务一套、后台准备另一套，验证后原子切换、旧的留回滚。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Blue-green deployment keeps two environments, one live and one prepared, swapping atomically after validation and keeping the old for rollback.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用新模型重嵌另建的一套索引，验证达标后整体替换旧索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A parallel index is a second index re-embedded with the new model, replacing the old one wholesale after validation.

scenario: 从原始文档到可检索索引，企业 RAG 的摄取管线要按固定顺序走完。
scenario_en: From raw documents to a searchable index, the enterprise RAG ingestion pipeline runs in a fixed order.
q: 把企业 RAG 的摄取管线排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the enterprise RAG ingestion pipeline correctly:
steps: 嵌入模型编码每个块(并打上模型版本标签)
结构感知解析，识别表格/标题/列表
写入向量索引(同批块也进 BM25 倒排索引)
why: 先结构感知解析保住表格/标题→按策略分块→嵌入并打版本标签→写入向量索引(同一批块也建 BM25 倒排索引)。解析时并行抽取 ACL 元数据附到块上，供检索期做权限过滤。
why_en: Structure-aware parsing preserves tables/headers first → chunk by strategy → embed and tag the version → write to the vector index (the same chunks also build a BM25 inverted index), while parsing extracts ACL metadata in parallel for query-time permission filtering.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  R["原始文档"] --> P["结构感知解析"] --> C["分块"] --> E["嵌入+版本标签"] --> I[("向量索引 + BM25")]
  P -.并行.-> ACL["抽取 ACL 元数据"] --> C

termDefinitions.meaning: 从词映射到含该词文档的索引，BM25 词法检索的底层结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index maps terms to the documents containing them, the structure underlying BM25 lexical retrieval.

scenario: 5 万员工里，法务文档只有法务能看，检索绝不能把无权限的块返回给其他人。
scenario_en: Among 50k employees, legal docs are legal-only, and retrieval must never return unauthorized chunks to others.
q: 权限(ACL)信息在摄取管线的哪一步、怎么处理？
q_en: Where and how is permission (ACL) info handled in the ingestion pipeline?
why: 解析时并行抽取 ACL 元数据，在建索引前附到每个块上；这样检索期能按用户权限过滤块，restricted 内容不会外泄。权限是数据侧就要埋好的，不能等生成时再补。
why_en: Extract ACL metadata in parallel during parsing and attach it to each chunk before indexing, so retrieval can filter chunks by the user's permissions and restricted content never leaks — permissions are baked in on the data side, not patched at generation.
options: 权限只在 LLM 生成时用 prompt 提醒，不进数据管线
权限在查询时现算，不用预先附到块上
解析时并行抽取 ACL 元数据，建索引前附到每个块上，检索期按权限过滤，防越权泄露
权限交给前端控制，后端索引一律不管
options_en: Permissions are only reminded via prompt at generation, not in the data pipeline.
Permissions are computed live at query time, not pre-attached to chunks.
Extract ACL metadata in parallel during parsing, attach to each chunk before indexing, filter by permission at retrieval to prevent leakage.
Permissions are handled by the frontend; the backend index ignores them.
optionExplanations: 靠 prompt 提醒挡不住检索层泄露，无权限的块一旦被召回就已经进了上下文。
现算权限而块上没有 ACL 元数据，就没有可过滤的依据，容易漏过。
对；ACL 在解析时抽好、随块入库，检索期直接按权限过滤，是防越权泄露的正确位置。
只靠前端控制形同虚设，后端能召回的就可能泄露，权限必须在检索层强制。
optionExplanations_en: A prompt reminder can't stop retrieval-layer leakage; once an unauthorized chunk is retrieved it's already in context.
Computing permissions live without ACL metadata on the chunk leaves nothing to filter on, so leaks slip through.
Correct — ACLs are extracted at parsing and stored with chunks, so retrieval filters by permission, the right place to prevent leakage.
Frontend-only control is hollow; whatever the backend can retrieve may leak, so permissions must be enforced at retrieval.

termDefinitions.meaning: 访问控制列表：规定谁能访问某资源，附到块上用于检索期权限过滤。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ACL (Access Control List) specifies who may access a resource, attached to chunks for permission filtering at retrieval.

scenario: 用户查「Section 14.2(b)」这种精确条款号时，稠密向量检索返回一堆语义相关但不是这条的条款；而查「合同能不能提前解约」这种改述，BM25 又抓不到。
scenario_en: For an exact clause like 'Section 14.2(b)', dense retrieval returns semantically related but wrong clauses, while for a paraphrase like 'can we terminate early', BM25 misses it.
q: 稠密 ANN 和 BM25 各自强在哪、弱在哪？
q_en: Where do dense ANN and BM25 each excel and fail?
why: 稠密 ANN 擅长语义相似(改述、近义)但漏精确关键词(产品码、条款号、缩写)；BM25 擅长精确词法匹配但对改述无能为力。两者互补，所以要混合检索同时用。
why_en: Dense ANN excels at semantic similarity (paraphrase, synonyms) but misses exact keywords (product codes, clause numbers, acronyms); BM25 nails exact lexical matches but fails on paraphrase — complementary, so use hybrid retrieval.
tradeoff: 稠密 ANN(懂语义但漏精确词) vs BM25(精确词法但不懂改述)
diagram:
flowchart LR Q["查询"] --> A["稠密ANN
语义"] Q --> B["BM25
精确词法"] A --> F["融合排序"] B --> F
options: 稠密 ANN 精确词法强、BM25 语义强，正好相反
稠密 ANN 懂语义/改述但漏精确关键词；BM25 精确词法匹配但不懂改述，二者互补
两者能力一样，选一个用就够
BM25 已过时，只用稠密 ANN 即可
options_en: Dense ANN is strong at exact lexical and BM25 at semantics — the reverse.
Dense ANN gets semantics/paraphrase but misses exact keywords; BM25 matches exact lexical but misses paraphrase — complementary.
Both are equivalent; pick one.
BM25 is obsolete; use dense ANN only.
optionExplanations: 说反了：稠密强在语义、BM25 强在精确词法，条款号这种要靠 BM25。
对；一个懂改述近义、一个抓精确词，正因为盲区互补才要混合检索。
两者盲区不同，只用一个就会在另一类查询上大量漏召回。
精确条款号/产品码等场景恰恰要 BM25，稠密单独用会漏这类命中。
optionExplanations_en: Backwards: dense is strong at semantics and BM25 at exact lexical; clause numbers need BM25.
Correct — one handles paraphrase/synonyms, the other exact terms, and their complementary blind spots are why you use hybrid.
Their blind spots differ, so using one alone misses many hits on the other query type.
Exact clause numbers/product codes need BM25; dense alone misses those hits.

termDefinitions.meaning: 近似最近邻检索：在海量向量里毫秒级找语义相近的块，牺牲一点精确度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) search finds semantically nearby chunks among massive vectors in milliseconds, trading a little exactness.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把查询和块都嵌成向量，用向量距离找语义相近项。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dense retrieval embeds query and chunks into vectors and finds semantically close items by vector distance.

scenario: 决定同时用稠密和稀疏两路检索来覆盖语义匹配和精确匹配。
scenario_en: You decide to run both dense and sparse retrieval to cover semantic and exact matching.
q: 混合检索在查询时是怎么工作的？
q_en: How does hybrid retrieval work at query time?
why: 查询时并行搜稠密向量索引和 BM25 倒排索引，各返回一个排序列表，再用融合(RRF 或学习权重)把两个列表合成一个。一路补另一路的盲区，召回既覆盖语义又覆盖精确词。
why_en: At query time, search the dense vector index and the BM25 inverted index in parallel, each returning a ranked list, then fuse them (RRF or learned weights) into one, so each covers the other's blind spot for both semantic and exact recall.
options: 先跑 BM25，没结果才跑稠密，串行兜底
只跑稠密，BM25 仅作备份不参与排序
把两个索引物理合并成一个再搜
并行搜稠密向量索引和 BM25 倒排，各出排序列表，用融合合成一个
options_en: Run BM25 first, then dense only if empty — serial fallback.
Run dense only; BM25 is just a backup not in ranking.
Physically merge the two indexes into one and search that.
Search the dense vector index and BM25 inverted index in parallel, each returning a ranked list, fused into one.
optionExplanations: 串行兜底会漏掉「两路都该贡献」的情况，且加了一次串行延迟，不如并行融合。
只跑稠密就放弃了精确词法命中，条款号/产品码类查询照样漏。
两个索引结构不同(向量 vs 倒排)，物理合并不成立，做法上就错。
对；两路并行各出榜、再融合，是混合检索的标准工作方式，兼顾语义与精确。
optionExplanations_en: Serial fallback misses cases where both lists should contribute and adds serial latency, worse than parallel fusion.
Dense-only abandons exact lexical hits, still missing clause-number/product-code queries.
The two indexes are structurally different (vectors vs inverted), so physically merging them isn't valid.
Correct — both search in parallel and their lists are fused, the standard hybrid method covering semantics and exact matches.

termDefinitions.meaning: 并行跑稠密与 BM25 两路检索，再融合两个排序列表取长补短。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hybrid retrieval runs dense and BM25 in parallel and fuses their ranked lists to combine strengths.

scenario: RAG 刚上线，还没有任何标注好的查询-文档相关性数据，你要先把两路检索的结果融合起来。
scenario_en: A RAG just launched with no labeled query-document relevance data yet, and you need to fuse the two retrieval lists.
q: 冷启动阶段该用哪种融合方法？
q_en: Which fusion method fits the cold-start stage?
why: 先用 RRF：它无参数、不用训练，靠 1/(k+rank) 把两路排名合并，是没有标注数据时的稳健基线。等积累了点击/相关性反馈，再训学习型融合权重去自适应领域。
why_en: Start with RRF: parameter-free and training-free, it merges the two rankings via 1/(k+rank), a robust baseline when there's no labeled data; once you accumulate click/relevance feedback, train learned fusion weights to adapt to the domain.
tradeoff: RRF(无需训练、即插即用但不自适应领域) vs 学习权重(自适应但要标注数据)
whenOtherWins: 当已有领域标注的查询-文档相关性对时，学习型融合权重能按领域(法务偏 BM25、对话偏稠密)自适应，超过无参数的 RRF。
options: 用 RRF：无参数、不用训练，靠 1/(k+rank) 合并两路排名，是无标注数据时的稳健基线
直接训学习型融合权重，哪怕没有任何标注数据也能训
只取稠密一路，放弃融合
人工每次手调两路权重
options_en: Use RRF: parameter-free, no training, merges the two rankings via 1/(k+rank) — a robust baseline with no labels.
Train learned fusion weights right away, even with no labeled data.
Take only the dense list and drop fusion.
Manually hand-tune the two weights every time.
optionExplanations: 对；没有标注就无法训权重，RRF 无参数即插即用，是冷启动阶段的稳健默认。
学习型融合要标注的查询-文档相关性对，没有数据根本训不出可信权重。
只取稠密丢掉精确词法命中，等于放弃混合检索的一半收益。
手调权重不可扩展、主观且难复现，不适合作为常规方案。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — with no labels you can't train weights, and RRF is parameter-free and plug-and-play, the robust cold-start default.
Learned fusion needs labeled query-document relevance pairs; without data you can't train trustworthy weights.
Dense-only drops exact lexical hits, forfeiting half of hybrid retrieval's benefit.
Hand-tuning weights doesn't scale, is subjective, and isn't reproducible as a standing method.

termDefinitions.meaning: 倒数排名融合：对每路名次取 1/(k+rank) 求和合并多路检索，无需训练。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RRF (Reciprocal Rank Fusion) merges retrieval lists by summing 1/(k+rank) across sources, needing no training.

scenario: RRF 的融合公式是 score(d) = Σ_r 1/(k + rank_r(d))，k 是个小常数。
scenario_en: RRF's fusion formula is score(d) = Σ_r 1/(k + rank_r(d)), with k a small constant.
q: RRF 这个公式怎么把多路排名合成一个分数，k 起什么作用？
q_en: How does the RRF formula merge multiple rankings into one score, and what does k do?
why: 对每个文档 d，把它在各路检索里的名次 rank 取 1/(k+rank) 再求和：名次越靠前贡献越大，多路都靠前的分最高。k 是小常数，压平头部名次之间的差距、降低单路极端排名的支配力，让融合更稳。
why_en: For each document d, sum 1/(k+rank) of its rank in each retriever: higher ranks contribute more, and items ranked high across lists score highest, while k, a small constant, flattens gaps among top ranks and curbs any single list's extreme rank from dominating.
options: 公式取各路 rank 里最大的那个数值，只认最差表现的那一路排名，其余各路排名忽略不计
公式把两路的原始分数直接相加，与名次无关
对每路名次取 1/(k+rank) 求和：越靠前贡献越大；k 是小常数，压平头部差距、防单路支配
是要背的公式，没有任何设计含义
options_en: Take only the maximum rank value across every retriever, using the single worst-ranked list and ignoring the rest of the rankings.
Sum the raw scores of the two lists, ignoring rank.
Sum 1/(k+rank) per list: higher ranks contribute more; k, a small constant, flattens top gaps and prevents single-list dominance.
A formula to memorize with no design meaning.
optionExplanations: 取最差那一路的名次等于让一票否决主导排序，一路排得再靠前也救不回来，这不是 RRF 的做法。
两路检索的原始分数量纲不同（余弦相似度 vs BM25 分），直接相加没有意义，这也是 RRF 改用名次的原因。
对；这正是 RRF 的算法本身，k 用来拉平第 1 名和第 3 名之间过大的分数差，让融合更平稳。
说它没有设计含义低估了它：这串公式直接决定谁能挤进候选前列，调错就调错了检索质量。
optionExplanations_en: Taking the worst rank lets one weak retriever veto everything — the opposite of what RRF is built to avoid.
Cosine and BM25 scores sit on different scales, so adding them raw is meaningless — why RRF works on rank instead.
Correct — that's literally what RRF computes; k softens the gap between top ranks so no single list dominates.
Calling it a rote formula undersells it — this sum decides the shortlist, so a wrong k skews retrieval quality.

termDefinitions.meaning: 文档在某一路检索结果里的排位，越靠前(数值越小)越相关。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Rank is a document's position in one retriever's result list; higher (smaller number) is more relevant.

scenario: 法务语料里，用户常查精确条款号(如「Section 14.2(b)」)；目前融合总把语义相关但错误的条款排在正确的精确匹配前面。
scenario_en: In a legal corpus, users often query exact clause numbers ('Section 14.2(b)'), but fusion keeps ranking semantically related wrong clauses above the exact match.
q: 该怎么修，让精确条款匹配排上去？
q_en: How do you fix this so exact clause matches rank higher?
why: 在领域标注的查询-文档相关性对上训学习型融合权重：法务这种精确匹配为主的语料要把 BM25 权重调高、稠密调低，让精确词法命中主导排序。RRF 无参数，做不到这种领域自适应。
why_en: Train learned fusion weights on domain-labeled query-document relevance pairs: for exact-match-heavy legal corpora, weight BM25 higher and dense lower so exact lexical hits dominate ranking — parameter-free RRF can't adapt like this.
tradeoff: 学习权重偏 BM25(精确匹配优先但要标注) vs 均等 RRF(无参数但不偏向精确)
whenOtherWins: 若是对话式知识库、查询多为改述，应把稠密权重调高；精确匹配没那么重要时，不必偏向 BM25。
options: 换个更大的 LLM，让它在生成时自己纠正排序
在领域查询-文档相关性对上训学习型融合权重，把 BM25 权重调高，让精确匹配主导
关掉 BM25，只留稠密检索
把 RRF 的 k 调到很大就行
options_en: Switch to a bigger LLM and let it self-correct ranking at generation.
Train learned fusion weights on domain query-document pairs, weighting BM25 higher so exact matches dominate.
Turn off BM25 and keep only dense retrieval.
Just set RRF's k very large.
optionExplanations: LLM 只能用检索给它的候选，排序错了、精确条款没进前列，生成阶段补不回来。
对；学习型融合能按领域把 BM25 权重抬高，让精确条款号命中主导，这正是 L5→Staff+ 的差别。
关掉 BM25 会连精确匹配的能力一起丢掉，与目标背道而驰。
调 k 只是整体压平名次差距，不能让精确匹配相对稠密获得更高权重。
optionExplanations_en: The LLM can only use retrieved candidates; if ranking is wrong and the exact clause isn't near the top, generation can't recover it.
Correct — learned fusion raises BM25's weight for the domain so exact clause hits dominate, the L5-to-Staff+ difference.
Turning off BM25 discards the exact-match ability entirely, opposite to the goal.
Tuning k only flattens rank gaps overall; it can't give exact matches higher weight relative to dense.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用小模型在标注相关性对上学最优的稠密/稀疏权重，按领域自适应。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Learned fusion trains a small model on labeled relevance pairs to learn optimal dense/sparse weights, adapting per domain.

scenario: 面试官问检索和重排各优化什么，想看你能否分清 recall 和 precision 的分工。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks what retrieval vs reranking each optimize, checking whether you separate recall from precision.
q: 检索(retrieval)和重排(reranking)分别优化什么？
q_en: What do retrieval and reranking each optimize?
why: 检索优化召回：宽撒网，把可能相关的都捞进候选集(宁多勿漏)；重排优化精度：在候选集里把真正最相关的排到前面(宁精勿滥)。融合后的候选集交给重排(下一课)，两阶段各司其职。
why_en: Retrieval optimizes recall: cast a wide net to pull all possibly-relevant chunks into the candidate set; reranking optimizes precision: within that set, push the truly most relevant to the top — the fused candidate set feeds reranking, each stage with its own job.
tradeoff: 检索(最大化召回、宽撒网) vs 重排(最大化精度、精排前列)
options: 两者都优化召回，重排只是跑得更快
检索优化精度、重排优化召回，正好相反
检索优化召回(宽撒网宁多勿漏)，重排优化精度(候选里把最相关的排前)
两者是同一步，不用分开
options_en: Both optimize recall; reranking is just faster.
Retrieval optimizes precision and reranking recall — the reverse.
Retrieval optimizes recall (wide net, don't miss), reranking optimizes precision (top-rank the most relevant in the set).
They're the same step, no need to separate.
optionExplanations: 重排优化的是精度不是召回，两阶段目标不同，不是快慢的差别。
说反了：检索管召回、重排管精度。
对；先宽召回再精排是两阶段设计的核心分工，一个保不漏、一个保排得准。
召回和精度目标不同、放一步会互相牵制，所以拆成检索+重排两阶段。
optionExplanations_en: Reranking optimizes precision, not recall; the two stages have different goals, not a speed difference.
Backwards: retrieval handles recall and reranking handles precision.
Correct — wide recall then precise reranking is the core two-stage split, one ensuring nothing is missed, the other ensuring correct ordering.
Recall and precision are different goals that fight in one step, which is why retrieval and reranking are split.

termDefinitions.meaning: 相关文档中被检索到的比例，检索阶段要最大化它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Recall is the fraction of relevant documents that get retrieved; the retrieval stage maximizes it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 返回结果中真正相关的比例，重排阶段要最大化它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Precision is the fraction of returned results that are truly relevant; the reranking stage maximizes it.

scenario: 索引因嵌入升级或分块变更要重建，但服务不能下线(5 万员工随时在用)。
scenario_en: The index must be rebuilt for an embedding upgrade or chunking change, but the service can't go down (50k employees always using it).
q: 怎么做到零停机重建索引？
q_en: How do you rebuild the index with zero downtime?
why: 蓝绿部署：两个索引槽，线上槽继续服务查询，离线槽在后台重建；新索引在 golden query set 上验证(recall@k、MRR)达标后，流量原子切换过去，旧槽留作回滚。全程不下线。
why_en: Blue-green deployment: two index slots, the live one keeps serving while the offline one rebuilds in the background; once the new index passes validation on a golden query set (recall@k, MRR), traffic swaps atomically and the old slot stays for rollback — no downtime.
tradeoff: 蓝绿(零停机可回滚但要双份索引资源) vs 原地重建(省资源但要停机)
whenOtherWins: 若只是日常加几篇新文档、模型没变，增量更新更快更省，不必整套蓝绿重建。
diagram:
flowchart LR L["蓝槽(线上)"] -->|服务查询| U["用户"] G["绿槽(离线重建)"] --> V{"golden set 验证
recall@k/MRR"} V -->|达标| SW["原子切流量"] L -.留作回滚.-> RB["旧索引"]
options: 直接在线上索引上原地改，边改边服务
停机几小时重建，贴公告让员工等
每次查询实时重新嵌入，不用预建索引
蓝绿：线上槽服务、离线槽重建，golden set 验证达标后原子切流量，旧槽留回滚
options_en: Edit the live index in place, serving while editing.
Take hours of downtime to rebuild and post a notice for employees to wait.
Re-embed live on every query, no prebuilt index.
Blue-green: live slot serves, offline slot rebuilds, atomic swap after golden-set validation, old slot kept for rollback.
optionExplanations: 原地改会在重建中途产生不一致状态，查询可能读到半新半旧的索引，质量抖动。
停机违背零停机硬要求，5 万员工随时依赖它，不可接受。
每次查询实时嵌入延迟爆炸，且失去索引意义，扛不住规模。
对；两槽切换让重建全程离线进行，验证达标才切、旧槽可回滚，是零停机重建的标准做法。
optionExplanations_en: In-place edits create inconsistent mid-rebuild states, so queries may read a half-new/half-old index with jittery quality.
Downtime violates the hard zero-downtime need with 50k employees depending on it — unacceptable.
Re-embedding per query explodes latency and defeats the index, unable to handle scale.
Correct — two slots let the rebuild happen fully offline, swapping only after validation with the old slot for rollback, the standard zero-downtime rebuild.

termDefinitions.term: golden query set / 黄金查询集
termDefinitions.meaning: 一组人工标好相关文档的代表性查询，用来验证新索引质量再切换。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A golden query set is a set of representative queries with hand-labeled relevant docs, used to validate a new index before swapping.

termDefinitions.meaning: 平均倒数排名：第一条正确结果名次倒数的平均，衡量排序质量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MRR (Mean Reciprocal Rank) averages the reciprocal rank of the first correct result, measuring ranking quality.

scenario: 索引更新有两种：每天加几篇新文档，或换嵌入模型后整体重嵌。
scenario_en: Index updates come in two kinds: adding a few new docs daily, or re-embedding everything after an embedding-model change.
q: 增量更新和全量重建各适合什么，代价是什么？
q_en: What do incremental updates and full rebuilds each fit, and at what cost?
why: 增量更新只把新文档加进现有索引，快、适合每日新增；但若中途换了嵌入模型，新向量来自不同模型，会累积 drift、向量空间不一致。全量重建重嵌整个语料保证所有向量一致，但很贵。
why_en: Incremental updates just add new docs to the existing index — fast, for daily additions — but if the embedding model changed, new vectors come from a different model and accumulate drift with an inconsistent space; a full rebuild re-embeds the whole corpus for consistency but is expensive.
tradeoff: 增量(快、省但换模型会 drift) vs 全量(一致但重嵌整库、贵)
options: 两者一样，随便用哪种都行
增量快、适合每日新增，但换模型会累积 drift；全量重嵌整库保一致但贵
增量最贵、全量最快，正好相反
增量会重嵌整库，全量只加新文档
options_en: They're the same; use either.
Incremental is fast for daily additions but accumulates drift if the model changes; full re-embeds the whole corpus for consistency but is costly.
Incremental is costliest and full fastest — the reverse.
Incremental re-embeds the whole corpus while full only adds new docs.
optionExplanations: 两者速度、适用和风险都不同，混用会在换模型时埋下 drift 隐患。
对；增量便宜但要求模型不变，全量贵但保证一致，选择取决于是否换了嵌入模型。
说反了：增量快而便宜、全量慢而贵。
颠倒了：增量只加新文档、全量才重嵌整库。
optionExplanations_en: They differ in speed, fit, and risk; mixing them plants drift when the model changes.
Correct — incremental is cheap but requires an unchanged model, full is costly but consistent, and the choice hinges on whether the embedding model changed.
Backwards: incremental is fast and cheap, full slow and expensive.
Reversed: incremental only adds new docs while full re-embeds the whole corpus.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只把新文档加进现有索引，快但要求嵌入模型不变。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An incremental update only adds new docs to the existing index — fast but requires an unchanged embedding model.

scenario: 团队一直用增量更新加新文档，期间悄悄把嵌入模型从 v1 换成了 v2，没有做整体重建。
scenario_en: A team keeps using incremental updates to add docs while quietly switching the embedding model v1→v2 without a full rebuild.
q: 这样长期下去会出什么问题？
q_en: What problem builds up over time here?
why: 增量加进来的是 v2 向量、老索引里是 v1 向量→同一索引里向量空间不一致→跨模型相似度失真→检索排序逐渐 drift、质量悄悄退化且难定位。修法是换模型时做全量重嵌，或走平行索引蓝绿切换。
why_en: Incrementally-added v2 vectors mix with old v1 vectors → an inconsistent space in one index → distorted cross-model similarity → retrieval ranking drifts and quality silently degrades, hard to trace — fix by full re-embedding on a model change or a parallel-index blue-green swap.
options: 新增 v2 向量与老 v1 向量混在一起→向量空间不一致→相似度失真→检索 drift、质量悄悄退化；换模型要全量重嵌
没问题，增量更新天然会对齐新旧模型
只会让索引体积变大，检索照常准确
会自动触发一次全量重建，无需担心
options_en: New v2 vectors mix with old v1 → inconsistent space → distorted similarity → retrieval drifts and quality silently degrades; a model change needs a full re-embed.
No problem; incremental updates naturally align old and new models.
It just enlarges the index; retrieval stays accurate.
It auto-triggers a full rebuild, so no worries.
optionExplanations: 对；这正是 drift 的成因，混着 v1/v2 让排序渐坏且隐蔽，换模型必须全量重嵌或平行切换。
增量更新不做任何跨模型对齐，混用只会累积不一致。
问题不在体积而在相似度失真，检索会实质变差。
系统不会自动重建，drift 会一直累积直到有人发现质量下滑。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — this is exactly how drift forms; mixing v1/v2 degrades ranking subtly, so a model change demands a full re-embed or parallel swap.
Incremental updates do no cross-model alignment; mixing only accumulates inconsistency.
The issue isn't size but distorted similarity, so retrieval materially worsens.
The system won't auto-rebuild; drift keeps accumulating until someone notices the decline.

termDefinitions.meaning: 索引里向量因模型不一致逐渐偏离，导致检索质量悄悄退化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Drift is the gradual divergence of index vectors from model inconsistency, silently degrading retrieval quality.

scenario: 要对 1000 万个块做全量重嵌，GPU 消耗很大，得控制成本。
scenario_en: You must fully re-embed 10M chunks with heavy GPU usage, and cost must be controlled.
q: 大规模全量重建怎么控成本？
q_en: How do you control the cost of a large full rebuild?
why: 放到业务低峰期、用 spot(抢占式)GPU 实例批量跑：全量重嵌是可容忍中断、非实时的离线批作业，spot 实例比按需便宜很多，低峰期跑不抢占在线资源。代价是 spot 可能被回收，作业要能断点续跑。
why_en: Run it as an off-peak batch on spot (preemptible) GPU instances: full re-embedding is a non-real-time, interruption-tolerant batch job, and spot is far cheaper than on-demand and off-peak avoids competing with online traffic, at the cost that spot can be reclaimed so the job must checkpoint and resume.
tradeoff: spot + 低峰(便宜但可能被回收) vs 按需实例(贵但不中断)
whenOtherWins: 若重建有硬性时限、不能被打断(如合规截止)，就得用按需实例保证不被回收，牺牲成本换确定性。
options: 用最贵的按需 GPU 实时跑，越快越好
在业务高峰期跑，反正集群有余力
低峰期用 spot 抢占式 GPU 批量跑：离线批作业可容忍中断，spot 便宜，作业要能断点续跑
干脆不重建，一直增量下去
options_en: Use the priciest on-demand GPUs in real time, faster is better.
Run it at peak hours; the cluster has spare capacity.
Off-peak batch on spot preemptible GPUs: a batch job tolerates interruption, spot is cheap, and the job must checkpoint and resume.
Just don't rebuild; keep going incrementally forever.
optionExplanations: 按需实例最贵，重嵌又不需要实时，用它是白花钱。
高峰期跑会和在线检索抢 GPU，抬高线上延迟，得不偿失。
对；离线批作业容忍中断，正好吃 spot 的低价+低峰的闲置，代价是要能断点续跑。
一直增量会在换模型时累积 drift，最终质量退化，不重建不是省钱是埋雷。
optionExplanations_en: On-demand is priciest and re-embedding isn't real-time, so using it wastes money.
Peak-hour runs steal GPUs from online retrieval, raising live latency — not worth it.
Correct — a batch job tolerates interruption, exactly fitting spot's low price and off-peak idle capacity, at the cost of checkpoint/resume.
Forever-incremental accumulates drift on model changes and ultimately degrades quality; not rebuilding buries a landmine rather than saving money.

termDefinitions.meaning: 云厂商的闲置算力，价格低但可能被随时回收，适合可中断的批作业。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A spot instance is a cloud provider's idle capacity at low price that may be reclaimed anytime, fit for interruptible batch jobs.

scenario: 新重建的索引要切上线前，得先过一道质量关，而不是切了再看。
scenario_en: Before a freshly rebuilt index goes live, it must pass a quality gate rather than being swapped in blind.
q: 索引切换前靠什么判断新索引够好、可以切？
q_en: What decides that a new index is good enough to swap in?
why: 用 golden query set(一组人工标好相关文档的代表性查询)在新索引上跑，量 recall@k 和 MRR 达标才切；这是不停机切换的质量闸门，达不到就不切、留在旧索引。
why_en: Run a golden query set (representative queries with hand-labeled relevant docs) against the new index and swap only if recall@k and MRR pass; it's the quality gate for zero-downtime cutover — if it fails, don't swap, stay on the old index.
options: 靠肉眼看几个查询，感觉还行就切
用 golden query set 跑新索引，量 recall@k 和 MRR 达标才原子切换，是切换的质量闸门
直接切，出问题再回滚就行
靠索引大小判断，越大越好
options_en: Eyeball a few queries and swap if it feels okay.
Run a golden query set against the new index and swap only if recall@k and MRR pass — the cutover quality gate.
Just swap; roll back if something breaks.
Judge by index size; bigger is better.
optionExplanations: 肉眼看几个查询没有量化判据，样本偏差大，挡不住质量回退。
对；用标好的黄金查询集量 recall@k/MRR，是可复现、可自动化的达标判据，达不到就不切。
先切再回滚会让用户短暂吃到坏索引，不如切前用黄金集拦住。
索引大小和检索质量无关，大的索引可能召回更差。
optionExplanations_en: Eyeballing a few queries has no quantitative criterion and heavy sampling bias, failing to catch regressions.
Correct — measuring recall@k/MRR on a labeled golden set is a reproducible, automatable pass criterion; if it fails, don't swap.
Swapping first and rolling back exposes users to a bad index briefly; better to gate before the swap with the golden set.
Index size is unrelated to retrieval quality; a bigger index can recall worse.

termDefinitions.meaning: 前 k 个结果里覆盖了多少真正相关的文档，衡量检索召回完整性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: recall@k is how many truly relevant documents appear in the top-k results, measuring retrieval completeness.

termDefinitions.meaning: 平均倒数排名：第一条正确结果名次倒数的平均，越接近 1 越好。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MRR (Mean Reciprocal Rank) averages the reciprocal rank of the first correct result; closer to 1 is better.
